entries.question: What is Tallyo?
entries.answer: Tallyo is a straightforward invoicing and business-records workspace. It keeps customers, quotes, invoices, payments and repeat invoicing together around your business.

entries.question: Who is Tallyo for?
entries.answer: Tallyo is designed for sole traders, freelancers, consultants, tradespeople and service companies that create quotes and invoices. It is built around your business rather than one particular trade.

entries.question: What can I do with Tallyo?
entries.answer: Tallyo supports invoices, quotes, credit notes, saved customers and items, branded PDFs, document email, payment tracking, recurring invoices, chosen overdue reminders, activity history, exports and account-protection controls. __TALLYO_CONNECT_PAYMENT_AVAILABILITY__

entries.question: How do I create an invoice or quote?
entries.answer: Choose the document type, add or select the customer, set the dates, add products or services and review the totals. Save the document, check its PDF, then email or download it when it is ready.

links.label: Create invoices, quotes and credit notes

entries.question: What is the difference between a quote and an invoice?
triggers: difference between a quote and invoice
entries.answer: A quote sets out proposed work and prices before the customer agrees. An invoice requests payment for agreed or completed work. Tallyo can create an invoice when a customer accepts a quote.

entries.question: What happens when a customer accepts a quote?
entries.answer: Tallyo keeps the accepted quote, records the confirmed customer name and acceptance time, and creates one linked invoice. The quote is not replaced or deleted.

entries.question: Can Tallyo send the invoice after a quote is accepted?
entries.answer: Yes, if automatic invoice email was selected before the quote was sent. You choose the due period and Tallyo uses the reviewed quote recipient. If automatic sending is off, or delivery fails, the linked invoice remains a Draft for you to review and send.

entries.question: What is a credit note?
triggers: when to use a credit note
entries.answer: A credit note records a reduction to an issued invoice. It keeps the original invoice and the adjustment visible instead of treating the original document as if it never existed.

entries.question: Can I save products and services?
entries.answer: Yes. Save products or services with their usual description and price, then reuse them on later documents. You can also create a new saved item while editing an invoice.

entries.question: Can I save customer details?
entries.answer: Yes. Saved customer records can be reused on documents. A customer page brings together balances, recent documents, recurring schedules and recent activity without turning Tallyo into a full CRM.

entries.question: Can I import customers from a CSV file?
entries.answer: Yes. The Customers page reads the CSV locally, shows a preview and asks for confirmation before adding valid rows. It skips invalid rows and duplicate email addresses and does not overwrite existing customers.

entries.question: Can I add a percentage or fixed discount?
entries.answer: Yes. In the Tallyo app you can apply a percentage discount or enter a specific fixed amount, which is useful when you want the document total to reach an exact value.

entries.question: How do the tax modes work?
entries.answer: Choose Add tax on top when the entered price is before tax. Choose Prices include tax when the entered price already contains tax. Tallyo then shows the line and document totals using that choice.

entries.question: How do recurring invoices work?
entries.answer: Save an invoice schedule, choose how often it runs, when it starts and ends, and whether each newly created invoice should be emailed automatically or left for review. You can pause or change the schedule when the work changes.

entries.question: How do overdue reminders work?
entries.answer: An invoice becomes overdue when its due date has passed and money is still owed. Tallyo sends reminders only for invoices where you turned reminders on; it does not email every overdue invoice automatically.

entries.question: How do I record a payment?
entries.answer: Open the invoice Payments section and add the amount, date and a short note for money received by bank transfer, cash or another agreed method. Tallyo updates the amount still left to pay.

entries.question: Can I record a deposit or part-payment?
entries.answer: Yes. Add a deposit or part-payment to the invoice and Tallyo shows the amount paid and the balance still left. Add the remaining amount later to show the invoice as fully paid.

entries.question: How does Tallyo show what is paid and still due?
entries.answer: Each recorded deposit, part-payment or final payment stays with the invoice. Tallyo shows the total paid, the amount still due and whether the invoice is paid, due or overdue.

entries.question: Can customers pay by card?
triggers: how do stripe card payments work
entries.answer: __TALLYO_CONNECT_PAYMENT_FAQ__ You can also record payments received through another agreed route.

entries.question: Does Tallyo store card details?
entries.answer: Tallyo does not store payment-card details. When card payments are available for your account, Stripe hosts checkout and handles the card information.

entries.question: How do refunds work?
entries.answer: For a Stripe card payment confirmed in Tallyo, use the invoice refund action; Tallyo asks Stripe to process the refund and updates the invoice after signed confirmation. For payments received another way, refund through that route and keep the invoice record consistent.

entries.question: What does activity history show?
entries.answer: Activity history shows when a document was created or sent, when reminders went out and when payments were recorded. It is a useful product record, not a tamper-proof compliance audit log.

entries.question: Can I check whether a document email was delivered?
entries.answer: Tallyo records the result returned by the email service and shows related events in the document activity. An accepted or delivered provider event helps with follow-up, but cannot guarantee that a person read the message.

entries.question: Can I add my logo and brand colours?
entries.answer: Yes. In Branding you can add your logo, choose its position and select your brand colour while a live document preview shows the result. Tallyo keeps headings and totals readable even when the chosen colour is light.

links.label: See branding in the product tour

entries.question: Which invoice templates can I choose?
entries.answer: Tallyo includes four document layouts: Tallyo, Basic, Modern and Professional. Choose the style in Branding and use the live preview to see how it presents your business details, items and totals.

entries.question: Can I turn alternating item colours off?
entries.answer: Yes. Branding includes a preference for alternating item-row colours. Leave it on for white and tinted rows, or turn it off for one consistent item background.

entries.question: Can I export my records?
entries.answer: Yes. Tallyo offers spreadsheet export for document lists and a structured account export for records associated with your account. Downloaded files are outside Tallyo's technical control, so store them appropriately.

entries.question: What can the Free Invoice Maker do?
entries.answer: The Free Invoice Maker works in your browser without an account. Add business and customer details, line items, discounts, tax, payment details and a local logo, then preview, print or save the finished document as a PDF.

entries.question: What is not included in the Free Invoice Maker?
entries.answer: The Free Invoice Maker does not save customer or service records to an account and does not include Tallyo email sending, document history, payment tracking, recurring invoices, reminders, cloud account storage, credit notes or online payments.

entries.question: Can I install Tallyo?
entries.answer: Yes. Open the Tallyo app by choosing Log in or Create account. On Chrome or Edge on a computer, look for the install or app symbol at the right end of the address bar. On Android Chrome use the three-dot menu. On iPhone or iPad Safari use the Page or Share menu, then Add to Home Screen.

entries.question: Can I use Tallyo on different devices?
entries.answer: Yes. Tallyo works in supported modern browsers on phone, tablet and computer and can be installed for quicker access. Authenticated business records still require an internet connection.

entries.question: Does Tallyo work offline?
entries.answer: The app shell can open offline, but an internet connection is required to sign in and access or update authenticated business records. Recurring schedules and reminders rely on Tallyo's connected services.

entries.question: How do I create an account?
triggers: how do i create an account
entries.answer: Choose Create account on the Tallyo website, enter your details in the Tallyo app and complete the email-confirmation step.

entries.question: How do I log in?
entries.answer: Choose Log in on the Tallyo website to open the app. Use your confirmed account and complete authenticator verification when you have enabled it.

entries.question: How can I protect my Tallyo account?
entries.answer: Confirm your email, use a strong unique password and optionally add authenticator-app multi-factor authentication. Keep one-time recovery codes safely away from your usual device and use the all-devices sign-out option if access may be at risk.

entries.question: How much does Tallyo cost?
entries.answer: The Free Invoice Maker costs £0 and requires no account. Tallyo Pro is £8 per month or £80 per year for one business and one user. You can choose a monthly or annual subscription from Tallyo.

entries.question: Do monthly and annual plans have different features?
entries.answer: No. Monthly and annual Tallyo Pro subscriptions include the same features. Annual billing costs £80 upfront and saves £16 compared with twelve monthly payments.

entries.question: Is there a free trial?
entries.answer: Tallyo does not currently offer a full-feature free trial. You can use the Free Invoice Maker without an account, or choose monthly billing as the lower-commitment way to evaluate the saved Tallyo workspace.

entries.question: What happens when I cancel Tallyo Pro?
entries.answer: Cancelling stops future renewal. Paid access normally continues until the end of the billing period already paid for, and existing records are not immediately deleted. Use the Stripe Customer Portal from your Tallyo account to cancel future renewal.

entries.question: Does Tallyo Helper have private account access?
entries.answer: No. Tallyo Helper is a public product guide. It cannot authenticate, inspect or change an account and has no access to Supabase, Stripe, Resend or private business records.

entries.question: What happens to a question I ask Tallyo Helper?
entries.answer: When the AI path is enabled, Tallyo sends only your current question and selected reviewed public guidance securely to OpenAI. Tallyo does not intentionally save the conversation, and the request uses store:false. Do not enter private business information or secrets.

entries.question: Does Tallyo replace accounting software?
entries.answer: No. Tallyo helps with invoicing and connected business records, but it is not a full accounting suite and does not prepare tax returns or provide legal, tax or accounting advice.

entries.question: How do I get support?
entries.answer: Start with the Help Centre guides and common questions. If you still need help, email main@tallyo.co.uk and never include passwords, authenticator codes, recovery codes, card details or bank details.

entries.question: Where can I read about security?
triggers: where can i read about security
entries.answer: The Security page describes Tallyo's current account, data-access, payment and browser controls together with honest limitations.
